strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation distinguishing proactive (SRGen) from reactive error correction approaches
Strong theoretical grounding through Theorem 1 showing the hybrid loss is equivalent to constrained optimization with Pareto-optimality interpretation
Comprehensive experimental validation across 4 diverse models (7B-32B, multiple architectures) and 6 benchmarks with consistent improvements
Practical plug-and-play applicability without training, demonstrable composability with other methods (SLOT), and bounded computational overhead
Thorough efficiency analysis (Section 5.3) showing overhead scales only with intervention count, not sequence length
Insightful analysis of triggered tokens (Section 5.6) validating that interventions target decision-critical function words rather than content tokens
Compelling demonstration that dynamic thresholding is necessary (Appendix F) with entropy profiles varying dramatically across models
Robust to hyperparameter variations (Appendix G: ±1% stability across reasonable ranges)
weaknesses: Moderate technical novelty—combines existing components (entropy detection, hidden state injection, dual-objective losses) rather than introducing fundamentally new mechanisms
Restrictive white-box requirement (hidden state and gradient access) severely limits real-world deployment on API-only production models, undermining practical claims

Design choices inadequately justified: (1) dynamic threshold form (µ+kσ) lacks comparison to alternative anomaly detection methods; (2) entropy minimization objective not compared to other uncertainty metrics; (3) uniform δ application to all historical states (Eq. 6) lacks ablation against localized variants
No quantitative analysis of intervention quality: missing false-positive rate, intervention success rate, and precision/recall of uncertainty detection
Theoretical assumptions not fully validated: coercivity for minimizer existence unverified; Joint-Descent Lemma's acute-angle requirement breaks down after early optimization steps (Fig. 9)

Experimental limitations: (1) no confidence intervals despite 'five runs'; (2) lack of significance testing with some improvements modest (e.g., +0.7±3.3 on AIME2025); (3) inconsistent decoding setup (greedy vs. temperature 0.6) across tables

Limited evaluation scope: all benchmarks are mathematics/reasoning-heavy; no evaluation on generation tasks (summarization, translation) where entropy patterns differ; function-word triggering pattern may be task-specific
Multiple hyperparameters (6 total: k, N, λ, T, η, τ) with non-obvious defaults; paper acknowledges 'best performance may vary' requiring per-task tuning
Missing critical ablations: alternative loss formulations, threshold mechanisms, contextual fidelity implementations, and temperature sensitivity beyond Appendix F

Incomplete technical specification: ring buffer initialization when |E| < N undefined, stopping criterion for δ optimization vague ('a few steps'), clarification of historical vs. current δ injection (Algorithm 1, line 15)
